speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe exactly where you feel the pain in your wrist and whether it radiates to your fingers or thumb. Have you noticed any recent swelling, redness, or an inability to make a fist?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given the radiation of pain to the elbow and your history of falling on an outstretched hand, are you currently able to fully extend your wrist or is there noticeable weakness? REQUEST IMAGES: Right_wrist_hand_Xray, Right_elbow_Xray.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic pain following a fall on the right outstretched hand.

I will review the X-rays to check for any underlying fractures, but your description of pain worsening with lifting your son suggests a soft tissue or tendon injury that may have been missed initially. Have you noticed any clicking or popping sounds in your wrist or elbow when moving them?
